title: Left-right randomization is concordant within an embryo except after VANGL knockdown

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Left-right randomization is concordant within an embryo except after VANGL knockdown

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Bioelectric and biochemical perturbations of vertebrate left-right patterning randomize laterality only at the level of whole embryos (each embryo's cells agree on L and R identity); the only known perturbation that breaks this concordance is down-regulation of planar-polarity VANGL signalling, which produces speckled L/R marker expression on both sides of the midline.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In all of the many studies on perturbation of the LR pathway, we are aware of only one that actually breaks the concordance: disruption of the planar polarity pathway by down-regulating VANGL signaling149 leads to a speckling on both sides of the midline, consistent with individual cells within a single lateral domain disagreeing on whether they should have L or R identity (Fig. 6a–d).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions”. Scope: Vertebrate embryos (chick, Xenopus and others) with perturbed left-right pathways

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Speckling versus side-level concordance is operationalizable from published spatial data. Existing literature can test many interventions, but heterogeneous reporting and the universal literature claim limit completeness.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Systematically code cell-level left/right marker concordance after each published pathway perturbation and compare VANGL knockdown with all other interventions under common spatial criteria.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The only-known qualifier requires a broad and updateable literature search.

Studies use different species, markers, stages, and image resolution.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Within-embryo concordance of left-right markers is visible in a large published in situ literature, and Xenbase indexes the Xenopus share of it, including VANGL. Extracting speckling versus isomerism across that literature is weeks to months of figure scoring, not a download of one table. Publication bias and an open-ended study list keep the 'only one perturbation' clause only partly decidable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across published left-right perturbations, score whether each embryo's lateral markers are concordant (situs solitus, inversus or isomerism) or speckled within a side, and treat VANGL knockdown as the proposed exception. Finding speckled discs under other published treatments would refute uniqueness; concordant outcomes everywhere except the VANGL reports would support the survey claim as far as the sampled literature goes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Concordant situs classes are what papers usually score, so speckling can be under-reported.

The survey is bounded by studies the authors know, not by a pre-registered sample.

Marker speckles can be staining noise rather than cells disagreeing about identity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.74
data existence: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.5
